facts.detail: Net neutrality, or the open internet, means users control what they see and do online rather than the ISP.
The rules protect equal and non-discriminatory treatment of internet-access traffic and end-user rights.
After the EU transition period ended, the open-internet rules became part of domestic UK law.
Ofcom monitors compliance in the UK and is required to publish an annual report.

guard_streams.write_limit: Open-internet rights and monitoring do not establish parcel coverage, speed or availability.

facts.detail: Ofcom published its UK net-neutrality framework review conclusions in October 2023.
The review found the framework generally worked well and supported consumer choice.
Ofcom also found the framework enabled content providers to deliver services to consumers.
Revised guidance explains how mobile and broadband providers should comply and how Ofcom assesses compliance.

guard_streams.write_limit: Framework findings and provider duties are regulatory evidence, not exact address data.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the public-interest exception clarification on 20 July 2026.
Existing guidance identifies fraudulent content and intimate-image abuse content as examples where targeted blocking may be acceptable.
Ofcom clarified that the public-interest exception list is not exhaustive.
Other harmful-content blocking is considered case by case and should be reasonable, proportionate, targeted and appropriately evidenced, with accessible error-reporting mechanisms.

guard_streams.write_limit: Traffic-management exceptions cannot be converted into parcel network measurements.

facts.detail: Since 1 October 2018, mobile providers must offer bill-limit options to new customers and customers entering or extending a contract.
A customer with a qualifying post-2018 contract can request a bill limit at any time.
A reasonable activation notice period should not exceed one billing period, usually one month.
A bill limit agreed before contract formation should apply from the start.

guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile billing protections do not prove fixed or mobile coverage at a parcel.

facts.detail: The mandatory bill-limit right applies to mobile phone services, not home phone or broadband.
It covers provider-supplied mobile calls, texts and data.
Paper-bill fees, late-payment fees and other non-mobile-service charges may be outside the limit.
The full cost of premium-rate or charge-to-mobile services need not be included, although the provider access charge must be covered.

guard_streams.write_limit: Cost-control scope cannot populate parcel serviceability or measured-speed fields.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom unwanted calls texts and emails

facts.detail: A live marketing caller must identify the company and provide a contact number.
If the consumer asks a live marketer to stop calling, the company must stop.
TPS-registered numbers should not receive live marketing calls unless the consumer specifically consented.
Automated marketing calls require explicit consent.

guard_streams.write_limit: Unwanted-contact rules are consumer protections, not network coverage evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom unwanted calls texts and emails; Ofcom tackling nuisance calls and messages

facts.detail: For a known sender or shortcode, consumers can reply STOP to opt out without a charge.
For an unknown sender, consumers should not reply and can forward the message to 7726 free.
The ICO leads on live telesales, automated marketing calls and spam texts.
Ofcom focuses on abandoned and silent calls and can enforce against persistent network misuse.

guard_streams.write_limit: Reporting channels and enforcement roles cannot identify exact parcel connectivity.

facts.detail: The Scottish Government is the contracting authority for local and regional Project Gigabit contracts in Scotland.
GoFibre is the awarded supplier.
The contract targets up to 10,700 premises across the Borders and East Lothian.
The BDUK guidance page was published on 21 February 2025 and directs users to Scottish Government contract detail.
